pathwayLabel: Full New Application Required — No Reciprocity or Exam Waiver Available for C-36
examName: CSLB C-36 (Plumbing) trade exam plus the California Law and Business exam — no waiver route exists for a Texas license
steps: Texas is not one of CSLB's reciprocal-agreement states (Arizona, Louisiana, Mississippi, Nevada, North Carolina) and does not appear on CSLB's Reciprocal Classifications List, so no reciprocity trade-exam waiver applies.
CSLB's NASCLA exam waiver does not help: it is restricted to the B-General Building classification and does not cover C-36.

California's other exam waiver (Business and Professions Code §7065.1) applies only to qualifiers of licenses issued by CSLB itself, not to out-of-state licenses — so a Texas Journeyman or Master Plumber license does not qualify.

Unlike the reverse direction, the difference in license type is not a barrier here: CSLB qualifies C-36 applicants on documented experience, not on holding a particular license. File CSLB's Application for Original Contractor License (form 13A-1) with the $450 non-refundable application fee, documenting at least four years of journey-level (or higher) C-36 experience within the last 10 years on CSLB's Certification of Work Experience form. Work as a Texas Journeyman or Master Plumber can count, but must be documented on CSLB's own form.
Once the application is posted, pass the C-36 trade exam and the California Law and Business exam; exam fees are paid directly to the testing vendor and are not published in the application.
After passing, pay the initial license fee ($200 sole owner / $350 non-sole owner) and file the required $25,000 contractor's bond with CSLB.
Await processing — CSLB does not publish a guaranteed timeline; budget for several weeks to a few months.
notes: Confirmed 2026-09-30 from live CSLB sources: the Reciprocity Requirements page lists five reciprocal states (Arizona, Louisiana, Mississippi, Nevada, North Carolina), none of them Texas, and limits the NASCLA waiver to General Building (B); the Reciprocal Classifications List has no Texas entry (that page also says "California and three other states" and names four, omitting Mississippi — an inconsistency on CSLB's own site that does not affect this pair). The C-36 classification is 16 CCR §832.36, read in full on CSLB's classification page. Fees, experience, bond and exam requirements are from CSLB form 13A-1 rev. 01/2026 (current PDF, downloaded and extracted directly): $450 application fee, $200/$350 initial license fee, four years of experience at no less than journeyman level within the last 10 years (T16 CCR §825), Law and Business plus trade exam (BPC §7065), $25,000 contractor's bond (BPC §7071.6). BPC §7065.1's exam waiver is limited to CSLB licensees ('licensee' per BPC §7096 = licensed under the Contractors chapter), so it does not reach a Texas license. The Texas side issues only individual plumber licenses (TSBPE Administrative Rules, March 2026, §365.1); that is not an obstacle in this direction because CSLB's eligibility test is experience-based. feeUsd is the application fee only and excludes the initial license fee and vendor exam fees.
